reading: read() is the only exact manuscript-content read path and is statelessly paged.
Each call returns at most 9000 content characters plus compact metadata.
Pass next_cursor back to read() until complete=true. The cursor identifies the requested item index and character offset.
context(), search(), and brainstorms() are navigation surfaces and do not substitute for exact paged reads.
research_contract: Startup is fully informed from the artifact; Main Lines are read last.
After choosing a route, use changes() only as a compact freshness/version signal. Page through only the chosen Main Line or Research Line if its version changed.
During mathematical research, workers self-police the no-consultation rule and keep intermediate reasoning local.
Publish only after substantial progress in one coherent staged batch.
review_staged_batch() is a required concurrency barrier; commit_staged_batch() refuses if another session publishes after review.
research_lines: A Research Line is read as one assembled manuscript but authored as ordered chunks.
Exactly one chunk is hot. Ordinary mathematical additions edit only that hot chunk with save_line_chunk().
Crystallization freezes the hot chunk and opens a new empty hot chunk without changing the line math_version.
Older crystallized chunks are normally not rewritten. When the line matures, compress the whole line by an explicit Main Line rewrite.
Direct Research Line body edits through save_research() are rejected; save_research() remains available for line metadata and Toolkit objects.
searching: search() matches full text across titles, simplified statements, statements, and bodies; documents are included by default.
Results are ordered primarily by match count per object.
filters.result_level may be ids, metadata, simplified, statement, or full; simplified is the default.

Each call returns one packed result page capped at 9000 characters. filters.offset is the number of complete packed pages to skip; use offset=1,2,... for later pages. A result that would cross a page boundary moves intact to the next page; only a result larger than an empty page is truncated.
Brainstorms remain opt-in with include_brainstorms=true. Superseded and archived research remain hidden by default.
usage: Call through the active project schema.
